Art title 1: What We Take In is What We Trust In
Artist Statement 1:
Jesus said believe in me. Then he said, I am living water, and if you drink of me, I will give you eternal life. David Gusik (author of much of the Bible commentaries in the scriptures) pointed out what an appropriate metaphor "drinking" is for belief. We decide if what we drink is trustworthy enough to put into your body. Sometimes we examine it, sometimes we don't. Perhaps we should examine more closely the things we fill our body with. 

What in your life have you taken inside of you, that you have taken on uninformed, or unexamined belief? 

Perhaps everyone else you see around you and in media are doing it? Perhaps it is based on what you want, but not what is good for you. Perhaps you want to stop drinking it in, but you do not know how. Let's try to get our sustenance from the rich, harrowing life of Jesus, and his life of pouring ourselves out while staying close to him, and may that fill us up so we do not turn to less trustworthy drink.

Hank Shepherd wrote a song that made him famous.  When he was only 21 "Momma's Eyes" Swept the charts and the hearts of the country-western world.  His mother raised him on the values of honesty and faithfulness until he was 17 when cancer whittled her into the grave.  And it was honesty and faithfulness that he was now known for.

The tabloids profited by painting Hank as overly ideal, ridiculously chivalrous, and unfashionably old fashioned.  Hank seemed to take no notice and simply, daily strove to be the man his mom had raised him to be.  His lyrics were never crude. He was considered a prude and a bore compared to the bands that he toured with. Though if you were to talk to any of them, they would each trust him more than they would their own band mates.  When the girls offered themselves to him after each show, he quietly passed out a flower or a kiss on the cheek to each before he disappeared into his trailer to work on his music.

When they asked him why was he so different, Hank always said something like, "there was just something special I saw in my momma's eyes."

He said she taught him everything it is to be a real man.  But the main thing he remembered from his mother was her patient endurance through a multitude of abusive men- all because she wanted to find him a good father.
